Subject: Order form expiry notification + fallback plan

Hi Laura / Archimedes procurement —

Quick note that the current order form tied to Acct: ACQ-2026-1937 is scheduled to expire on 2026-08-31. Legal has indicated the MSA and the order form are still under review, and we want to avoid an unexpected service interruption for your team.

Proposed low-friction approach:
- We can offer a 30-day extension on the existing order form to buy time for final sign-off (no service or billing changes).
- If you prefer to opt out of auto-renew, we can include language to disable auto-renew pending signature of new docs.
- As a fallback, Redwood can keep services active on a month-to-month arrangement while we finalize the MSA redlines (short-term pricing hold).

Asks / next steps:
1) Please confirm procurement's preferred path (30-day extension vs. pause auto-renew vs. month-to-month) by EOD Wed (2026-07-21).
2) If you want the 30-day extension, sign the attached extension addendum and return to procurement@redwood.com.

Kimberly / Ben — can you review the termination-for-convenience and notice-window redlines the Archimedes legal team flagged? I'll loop internal legal (Marissa) once we have their preference so we can propose specific language.

Thanks —
Jordan
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Order form expiry notification + fallback plan

Jordan — thanks for the heads up. Quick read on the flagged items:

- Term / Auto-Renew: Archimedes asked to remove automatic extension language unless both parties sign a new order. That's a commercial ask we can accommodate with a 60-day notice carve-out on our side.
- Notice window: their legal wants 30 days' notice to terminate for convenience; our standard is 60. We can offer a compromise of 45 days with a staggered refund schedule for prepaid credits.
- Termination for convenience: they want the ability to terminate mid-term without liability. We should retain a pro-rated payment mechanism and a short transition SLA (30 days).

I'll draft two short options to present:
A) 30-day extension + disable auto-renew until new OF signed (internal preferred if procurement needs speed).
B) 60-day auto-renew disable + 45-day notice compromise + pro-rated settlement (preferred for risk).

Marissa — can you confirm if Legal is comfortable with the pro-rated settlement language and the 45-day notice? If so I will populate redline options in the attached docx.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Head of Commercial Contracts
